episode.subject: striped frogfish on sand
episode.title: A firmer greeting
episode.body:
She came closer. I lifted a fin to wave.

The rest of me leaned after it.

Put it down quickly. She stopped.

I wanted her to know I hadn't changed my mind.

I moved one fin, then another, until I was facing her properly. Kept all four on the sand.

She came the last little distance.

proposals.visibleScene: Single orange hairy striped frogfish stands on sand with fin supports, face and lure sharply visible. No second fish visible. Full-body side angle better than close portraits for proposed balancing action.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Partner, approach, wave, momentary imbalance and repositioning are fiction. Still depicts stable support, not a photographed wave or fall. Four refers to paired pectoral and pelvic fin supports in established frogfish canon, not four pectoral fins. No changed color, broken lure or observed fish dialogue claimed.
proposals.continuity: If admitted insert after Crush beside the sponge before A mouthful of consequences. Preserve all18 original bodies and broken-lure chronology. Antennarius striatus matches actual avatar catalog classification; Lembeh source matches home. No new taxon or identity. Female companion may be established crush but not documented individual or sex.
proposals.review: Concrete original trial, not admitted. Main weakness is entirely unseen partner and sequence; body is a planted solitary frogfish. Physical response expresses continued interest instead of merely blushing, but independent editor must judge whether image earns it. Owner stop arrived before any additional biological source check; no new source work after stop.
